Zen 6 runs on one DGX Spark. Zen 6 Max wants a rack of Blackwell servers. What we measured, and what a rack is made of.
Zen 6 on one DGX Spark, as Hanzo measured it

A cold prompt of about that many tokens on a quiet box, measured Sep 20, 2026: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), 121 GiB unified memory, shared with the benchmark's other jobs; zen6, NVFP4 with FP8 attention, weights 21.6 GiB (serve-spark-zen6.sh).
NVIDIA DGX Spark: GB10, 273 GB/s memory bandwidth

We recommend at least four 8-GPU NVIDIA Blackwell servers, B300 or B200, for Zen 6 Max on your own premises. Routing cuts the average inference work a request needs. It does not cut the memory needed to keep every specialist ready.
NVIDIA DGX B300 user guide: 8 x 288 GB GPU memory
NVIDIA DGX B200 user guide: 1,440 GB total GPU memory
Four B300 servers hold 9,216 GB of GPU memory; four B200 servers hold 5,760 GB.
Four 8-GPU servers is where a qualification starts.
One pool for each specialist, so a busy class of work never takes memory from another.
Two independent replicas of those pools across failure domains.
NVLink and NVSwitch inside each server.
400 or 800 Gb/s RDMA wherever a specialist spans servers.
About 31 TB of NVMe in each server (8 x 3.84 TB).
Separate sandbox workers for coding agents.
Final capacity and performance commitments come from qualifying your workload: context length, concurrency, routing mix, latency, and failover.

Where do the savings figures come from?

Every rate is read from our price list and our plan list when the page opens; the volumes, the people and the GPUs are yours. The figure for your own GPUs counts them on all month at an hourly rate and leaves out the Enterprise agreement, which our team prices with you.
